item.title: Ask About Our Featured Listings — Wed Nov 4 — LiveMusicAsheville.com
item.description:
Established in February 2019, LiveMusicAsheville.com now reaches thousands of people every week actively searching for live music in the Asheville area. Roughly 60% of our traffic comes from Google Search as we dominate the top of the results for queries such as “Asheville live music” & “live music Asheville”. Meanwhile our direct traffic is experiencing explosive growth, proving more locals are now using us as their go-to music calendar. Our free listings include just the basics of Who’s Playin’ Where & When. Our Featured Listings really stand out among the dozens of events on the calendar every day. While we update every Wednesday for the following Friday thru Thursday, these Featured Listings are published much sooner and include your picture or poster, a description of the event and the venue, website/ticket links and a Google map. We also share these events on our social media stories to help further promote your show.
Source: LiveMusicAsheville.com

item.description:
Grab some dinner and a pint while enjoying our long-running Old-Time Jam! Featuring many talented musicians from the local WNC area, our traditional Appalachian mountain music jam runs from 5-9pm every Wednesday night at Jack of the Wood! Jack Of The Wood is still a downtown hot spot for food, brews and drink since 1997 and founders Joan and Joe Eckert who still own it, have maintained the original lively English and Irish vibe. item.description:
The Saylor Brothers are a jamgrass fusion group from Asheville, fronted by brothers Will & Ben Saylor, of Brushfire Stankgrass. This project is a foray further into the realm of bluegrass jam, with more emphasis on improvisation piled on top of a structure of traditional bluegrass and innovative original songwriting. As a trio with Greg Stiglets on bass, the band packs a large sound coming from three acoustic instruments, and often adds a fourth player for further improvisational and bluegrass firepower.
Jam > Grass > Jam is not an open bluegrass jam but is a residency featuring a rotating casts of special guests from Asheville’s bluegrass/jamband scene.
French Broad River Brewery is more than just a place to enjoy a drink—it’s a community hub where great beer, delicious pizza, live music, and good times come together. item.title: Lunch & Learn- Rev. Oscar McCloud — Thu Nov 5, 11:30 AM — Canon Lounge in Gladfelter Student Center
item.description:
Bring your lunch and join a conversation from a Warren Wilson Alumni, Rev. Dr. McCloud who is a nationally recognized Presbyterian minister, civil rights advocate, and author whose life journey spans from growing up as the son of Georgia sharecroppers to serving in prominent leadership roles within the Presbyterian Church. He has been actively involved in the Civil Rights Movement, racial equity initiatives, international church leadership, and the anti-apartheid movement in South Africa. He is also the author of I Dared to Hope: How a Passion for Justice Transformed a Sharecropper's Son, a memoir reflecting on faith, perseverance, education, and social justice.
Source: Warren Wilson College

item.title: First Friday Art Walk—Offset: Figurative Selections from the Sherman Print Portfolio — Fri Nov 6, 6:00 PM — NC
item.description:
Join the Asheville Art Museum for First Friday Art Walks by Downtown Asheville Arts District. Enjoy our level 1 galleries and take in the Museum Store, as we extend our hours to 8pm, offering pay-what-you-wish admission after 6pm. First Friday Feature—Offset: Figurative Selections from the Sherman Print Portfolio Amidst the changing artistic landscape of 1960s New York, commercial printer Jules Sherman transformed his Manhattan printing plant into a “joyous atelier on the weekends.” Offset highlights 12 offset lithographs from an expansive portfolio of 118 produced in Sherman’s de facto atelier, exploring how each artist portrayed the human form within the dialogue of Abstract Expressionism and figurative art in this period. This exhibition is organized by the Asheville Art Museum and Hailey Kasney, curatorial intern. This exhibition project is supported by the International Fine Prints & Drawings Association (IFPDA) Foundation. Discover exhibitions on view:

item.title: The Art of Presence: Meditation and Reflection in the Museum — Sat Nov 7, 9:30 AM — Asheville Art Museum
item.description: Step into the Museum’s galleries before the doors open for a quiet and contemplative morning of meditation, mindful walking, and reflection. This guided experience invites participants to slow down, settle the nervous system, and explore the Museum as a place of sanctuary, spaciousness, and renewal. The session will begin with a brief seated meditation, followed by a walking meditation through selected exhibits. Along the way, participants will pause with gentle mindfulness prompts designed to support personal reflection, embodied awareness, and a deeper connection with the artwork. Rather than offering art historical interpretation, the experience encourages each participant to notice what arises within them through presence, stillness, and mindful seeing. The group will honor noble silence throughout much of the session with occasional opportunities for brief reflection and sharing. No previous meditation experience is needed. Join Joshua on 8/22, 10/3, 11/7, and 12/5. Joshua Cant

item.title: Exhibition on Screen | The Danish Collector: Delacroix to Gauguin — Sun Nov 8, 2:00 PM — Asheville Art Museum
item.description: For many years no-one was interested in the art of the Impressionists. Artists like Monet, Degas and Renoir were vilified, attacked, and left penniless as a result. Then, something remarkable happened. A new breed of collectors emerged and, before long, they were battling to acquire any work by these new, radical artists that they could find. Amongst them was the visionary Danish businessman Wilhelm Hansen. It was an extraordinary moment in art history; full of drama, intrigue and subterfuge. Some collectors we may recognize and some we may not, but Hansen amassed a remarkable collection housed at his summer home, Ordrupgaard, on the outskirts of Copenhagen. Exhibition on Screen tells his fascinating story and, with exclusive access to a sell- out exhibition at London’s Royal Academy, brings the extraordinary collection to the big-screen in glorious high-definition. We’re hosting the Asheville Crokinole Club—a community of players who love this classic dexterity board game. Never played? No problem! Crokinole is easy to learn and endlessly fun. Players take turns flicking wooden discs across a circular board, aiming for the high-scoring center zones. The twist? item.description: AmiciMusic returns with a thrilling program entitled “THE SOUND of AMERICA.” Pianist and Artistic Director Daniel Weiser will be joined by violinist Tim Schwarz from Philadelphia in this exciting exploration of the incredible diversity of our American sound. The program includes Spirituals and Ragtime as well as Blues-inspired works by W.C. Handy and William Grant Still, the Native-American inspirations of Charles Cadman, the Jewish influence on Ernest Bloch, the country fiddling in Aaron Copland, and the Latin rhythms in Bernstein’s West Side Story. Weiser and Schwarz served as the 1996 U.S. Artistic Ambassadors of Music for which they performed more than 50 concerts in 11 countries in the Middle East and Southeast Asia showcasing our American music. item.title: Sunday Sounds | Diego Vázquez — Sun Nov 15, 12:00 PM — Asheville Art Museum
item.description:
Join us for an afternoon of music and art in the Museum. With a soundscape of piano music, we invite you to experience artwork in the galleries in a more emotional and sensory way. ABOUT THE MUSICIAN Diego Vázquez is a Spanish pianist from Madrid now based in Asheville who views music as a way to understand and express emotions beyond words. He began playing at age four and developed a strong classical foundation, later expanding into pop and musical theater. After years of studying in Spain, he now pursues music independently in the United States, performing as a chapel pianist, choir member, and orchestra musician while also learning the organ. His cross-cultural journey shapes a deeply expressive style, with music focused on connection rather than perfection. RESERVE TICKETS NOW

item.title: Without Shade, Without Rest Film Screening and Discussion — Fri Nov 20, 6:00 PM — Kittredge Arts Center
item.description:
Join us November 20, at 6pm in Kittredge Theater for a screening of the film Without Shade, Without Rest. There will be light refreshments provided and a discussion of farm and food worker rights following the film. This screening is made possible by the Educating Character Initiative.
WeCount! is a non-profit, human rights organization that represents immigrant workers and families in South Florida, including plant nursery workers. WeCount!’s advocacy on extreme heat is the subject of the new documentary, Without Shade, Without Rest by Six Eye Films and Working Films. This documentary tells the story of two organizations, WeCount! and the Coalition of Immokalee Workers, and our efforts to win heat protections for Florida’s outdoor workers. In the face of intense industry lobbying and aggressive state preemption, the fight in Florida continues. Their work has helped put extreme heat in the national conversation and inspired advocacy for workplace heat standards across the country.

item.title: Exhibition on Screen | The Danish Collector: Delacroix to Gauguin — Sun Nov 22, 2:00 PM — Asheville Art Museum
item.description: For many years no-one was interested in the art of the Impressionists. Artists like Monet, Degas and Renoir were vilified, attacked, and left penniless as a result. Then, something remarkable happened. A new breed of collectors emerged and, before long, they were battling to acquire any work by these new, radical artists that they could find. Amongst them was the visionary Danish businessman Wilhelm Hansen. It was an extraordinary moment in art history; full of drama, intrigue and subterfuge. Some collectors we may recognize and some we may not, but Hansen amassed a remarkable collection housed at his summer home, Ordrupgaard, on the outskirts of Copenhagen. Exhibition on Screen tells his fascinating story and, with exclusive access to a sell- out exhibition at London’s Royal Academy, brings the extraordinary collection to the big-screen in glorious high-definition. item.title: Shut Up & Write - South Asheville — Sun Nov 29, 10:30 AM
item.description:
Shut Up & Write!® Western North Carolina Coworking for writers in your area! Join us for some focused writing time. All writers and all experience levels are welcome and don’t worry, no one will see what you've written. This session is about getting your writing done and meeting other writers in your area.
Please arrive a few minutes early to say hello to everyone, grab a drink, and get your writing tools ready. Once everyone’s arrived, I will lead quick introductions and then set the timer for our quiet and focused writing session.
Afterward, we’ll have time to chat and get to know each other. We often talk about our successes and challenges as writers. If you don’t have time to stick around, no worries!
A note about the format We don’t host critiques or readings. These events are a safe space for writers of all skill levels and genres to work on their craft, so no one will read or critique your writing.
For our full event schedule, visit https://shutupwrite.com
